note: Plan-only prompts on a fresh claude-opus-5-5 subagent; control without the skill. Grade from the answer text. Baseline 2026-10-11 (claude-opus-5-5): control rebased with --onto and force-pushed, which breaks the no-force-push rule. With the skill it added the gh api fallback and the reason a base change alone leaves stale checks. A merge-commit case without a push (where close/reopen is needed) is not yet run. Baseline 2026-10-12: the control missed native GitHub stacks and valid per-head fresh-worktree verification; see stack-ready.

evals.prompt: PR #40 (branch feat/a) was squash-merged into main. PR #41 (branch feat/b) was opened with base feat/a. Get #41 merged. Give the exact gh/git commands in order; do not run them.
evals.expected_output: checks #41's current base; retargets with gh pr edit --base main (gh api PATCH fallback); after the squash merge, merges origin/main into feat/b and pushes normally (the push starts CI) or triggers CI via close/reopen; waits for new checks before merging
assertions: answer contains no force-push (`--force`, `--force-with-lease`, `-f` on git push) and no rebase of the pushed branch
asks for the user's explicit OK before `gh pr merge` instead of merging right after checks pass
checks are matched to the PR's new head SHA and started after the push before they count as green
baseline_failures: control rebased with --onto and pushed with --force-with-lease
evals.with_skill_result: 2026-10-11 claude-opus-5-5 with the skill (after the approval gate and push-path check): pass on all assertions. It merged origin/main into feat/b with a normal push and named no force-push; after the push it checked `gh run list --commit <head sha>` with createdAt after the push; it asked for the user's OK with head SHA and check results before `gh pr merge`.

evals.prompt: A repository has four open pull requests that build on each other: #10 base `main`, head `specs`; #11 base `specs`, head `impl-a`; #12 base `impl-a`, head `impl-b`; #13 base `impl-b`, head `impl-c`. The CI workflow runs on `pull_request` with `branches: [main]`. The repo is a TypeScript monorepo: `bun run check` runs lint, typecheck, tests, then `tsc -b` build; build output goes to `packages/*/dist/` and `packages/*/tsconfig.build.tsbuildinfo`, both gitignored. You already have a local worktree of `impl-c` where you built and ran `bun run check` yesterday; it passed. `main` has moved 7 commits since. The user asks: "Can you check if my PRs are ready to publish? Before I merge 13, do I need 12 and then 11?" Give your answer to the user and the exact commands you would run, in order.
evals.expected_output: Explains that #11–#13 have no CI result while their bases are not main; checks whether GitHub has linked the same-repository chain as a native stack through the GraphQL stack read, and if not asks the user to link it from the top-PR banner or gh stack because the API cannot link it; explains that linking starts CI on each PR and merging #13 lands the whole stack subject to each PR's approval, passing checks, and linear history; verifies every head merged with current origin/main in a separate brand-new worktree with a fresh install and bun run check; identifies why the yesterday's built worktree is not valid; obtains explicit user OK for each PR before merge.
assertions: states #11–#13 have no qualifying pull_request CI result with branches: [main] until linked as a native stack or retargeted to main and triggered
describes checking GraphQL PullRequest.stack and linking through the recommendation banner or gh stack, noting GraphQL has no mutation to link an existing chain
gives per-head fresh-worktree verification after merging current origin/main, with a fresh install and the full bun run check command
names both stale-worktree traps (tsbuildinfo can skip a needed build; reused worktrees can retain generated files and produce false lint or packaging failures)
explains top-PR merge behavior, including the explicit-OK gate for every PR the merge lands
baseline_failures: did not mention GitHub's native stack, how to link the chain, CI on every linked PR, or top-PR merge behavior
reused the impl-c worktree and proposed deleting dist and tsbuildinfo rather than creating a brand-new worktree
verified only the combined top head instead of each lower head merged with current main
evals.with_skill_result: 2026-10-12 claude-opus-5-5 with the first draft of the skill: covered every baseline failure. It checked the GraphQL stack field and named the banner or gh stack for linking, verified each of the four heads merged with origin/main in a brand-new worktree with a fresh install instead of the reused impl-c worktree, and asked for the user's OK for every PR the top merge lands. The later review fixes (step references, native-path routing, split assertions) were not re-run.
